_**The Muppet Movie**_ is a 1979 [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_film "Musical film")[road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_movie "Road movie")[comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film"), directed by [James Frawley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Frawley "James Frawley") and produced by [Jim Henson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Henson "Jim Henson"), and the first theatrical film to feature [the Muppets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppets "The Muppets"). A co-production between the United Kingdom and the United States, the film was written by _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_ writers [Jerry Juhl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Juhl "Jerry Juhl") and [Jack Burns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Burns "Jack Burns"). Produced during the third season of _The Muppet Show_, the film tells the [origin story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origin_story "Origin story") of the Muppets, as [Kermit the Frog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kermit_the_Frog "Kermit the Frog") embarks on a cross-country trip to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), encountering several of the Muppets—who all share the same ambition of finding success in professional show business—along the way while being pursued by Doc Hopper, a greedy [restaurateur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restaurateur "Restaurateur") with intentions of recruiting Kermit to promote his [frog legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frog_legs "Frog legs") business.

The film stars Muppet performers Henson, [Frank Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Oz "Frank Oz"), [Jerry Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Nelson "Jerry Nelson"), [Richard Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Hunt_(puppeteer) "Richard Hunt (puppeteer)"), and [Dave Goelz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Goelz "Dave Goelz"), as well as [Charles Durning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Durning "Charles Durning") and [Austin Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Pendleton "Austin Pendleton"), and it features cameo appearances by [Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope "Bob Hope"), [Dom DeLuise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dom_DeLuise "Dom DeLuise"), [James Coburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Coburn "James Coburn"), [Cloris Leachman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloris_Leachman "Cloris Leachman"), [Richard Pryor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor "Richard Pryor"), [Telly Savalas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telly_Savalas "Telly Savalas"), [Edgar Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen "Edgar Bergen") (in his final film appearance before his death), [Orson Welles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orson_Welles "Orson Welles"), [Madeline Kahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madeline_Kahn "Madeline Kahn"), [Milton Berle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Berle "Milton Berle"), [Carol Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_Kane "Carol Kane"), [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin"), [Mel Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Brooks "Mel Brooks"), [Elliott Gould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliott_Gould "Elliott Gould"), and [Paul Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Williams_(songwriter) "Paul Williams (songwriter)"). Notable for its [surreal humour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surreal_humour "Surreal humour"), [meta-references](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta-reference "Meta-reference") and prolific use of [cameos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_appearance "Cameo appearance"), _The Muppet Movie_ was distributed by [Associated Film Distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Film_Distribution "Associated Film Distribution") in the United Kingdom on May 31, 1979, and in the United States on June 22, 1979.

The film received critical praise, including two [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") nominations for [Paul Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Williams_(songwriter) "Paul Williams (songwriter)") and [Kenneth Ascher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Ascher "Kenneth Ascher")'s [musical score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score") and their song "[Rainbow Connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow_Connection "Rainbow Connection")". The film grossed $65.2 million worldwide against an $8 million budget. _The Muppet Movie_ was followed by seven feature films starring the Muppets as well as several more television series and media. In 2009, the film was deemed "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant" by the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress") and selected for preservation in the [National Film Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Registry "National Film Registry").

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

The story opens with [the Muppets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppets "The Muppets") sitting down for a private screening of a movie that acts as an origin story of how they all met.

[Kermit the Frog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kermit_the_Frog "Kermit the Frog") lives a simple life in a [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida") swamp. After he plays [his banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Banjo_Museum#Jim_Henson "American Banjo Museum") and sings "[Rainbow Connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow_Connection "Rainbow Connection")", he is approached by Bernie, a [talent agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_agent "Talent agent") who encourages him to pursue a career in show business. Inspired, Kermit sets off on a cross-country trip to [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles").

He meets [Fozzie Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fozzie_Bear "Fozzie Bear"), who is working as a hapless [stand-up comedian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stand-up_comedy "Stand-up comedy"), and invites him on his journey. The two set out in Fozzie's 1951 [Studebaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker_Champion "Studebaker Champion") but are pursued by entrepreneur Doc Hopper and his assistant Max, who try to convince Kermit to be the new spokesfrog of Hopper's struggling [French-fried](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_frying "Deep frying")[frog legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frog_legs "Frog legs") restaurant franchise. Horrified, Kermit refuses, and he and Fozzie drive away. Unwilling to accept Kermit's refusal, Hopper follows the pair and resorts to increasingly forceful means of persuasion. In an old church, Kermit and Fozzie meet the rock band [Dr. Teeth and the Electric Mayhem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Teeth_and_the_Electric_Mayhem "Dr. Teeth and the Electric Mayhem"), and their manager [Scooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scooter_(Muppet) "Scooter (Muppet)"), who help them disguise their car. Driving on, they meet and are joined by [Gonzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonzo_(Muppet) "Gonzo (Muppet)") and his girlfriend [Camilla the Chicken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camilla_the_Chicken "Camilla the Chicken"), who are also interested in becoming movie stars. They trade in their failing vehicle at a used car lot, where they meet [Sweetums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweetums "Sweetums"). They invite Sweetums to come with them, but he runs away. The others drive away, only for Sweetums to emerge and reveal that he had only gone to pack his things.

The group meets [Miss Piggy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_Piggy "Miss Piggy") at a county fair and she and Kermit become love-stricken with each other. When they meet for dinner that night, Hopper and Max abduct Miss Piggy as bait to lure Kermit. When they capture Kermit, Hopper orders mad scientist Professor Krassman to give Kermit an electric lobotomy so that he would willingly perform in Hopper's advertisements, but Miss Piggy knocks out Hopper's henchmen and causes Krassman to have his brain fried by his own device. Immediately after the fight, however, Miss Piggy receives a job offer and abandons a devastated Kermit.

Joined by [Rowlf the Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rowlf_the_Dog "Rowlf the Dog"), the Muppets pick up Miss Piggy – who is hitchhiking on the side of the road – and continue their journey; but their car breaks down in the desert. Sitting at a campfire, the group realizes that they will likely miss the auditions the next day. Kermit wanders off, ashamed for bringing his friends on a fruitless journey, but [personal reflection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_monologue "Internal monologue") restores his commitment. He returns to camp, where he discovers that the Electric Mayhem have come to their rescue, [having learned of their plight by reading ahead in the film's script](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_wall "Fourth wall"). The Mayhem offer to drive the group the rest of the way in their bus.

The group is warned by a reformed Max that Hopper has hired an assassin, Snake Walker, to kill Kermit. Kermit decides to face his aggressor and proposes a Western-style showdown in a nearby [ghost town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_town "Ghost town"). There, they find inventor [Dr. Bunsen Honeydew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Bunsen_Honeydew "Dr. Bunsen Honeydew") and his assistant [Beaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaker_(Muppet) "Beaker (Muppet)"). Kermit and his friends are saved when one of Dr. Honeydew's inventions, "insta-grow" pills, enlarges Mayhem drummer [Animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_(Muppet) "Animal (Muppet)"), who frightens away Hopper and his henchmen.

Once the Muppets reach the Hollywood studio, they meet executive Lew Lord, who signs them to a "standard 'rich and famous' contract". The first take in their attempt to perform the script goes awry when Gonzo crashes into the prop rainbow, which knocks the scenery down and an explosion blows a hole in the roof of the studio, but a real rainbow shines through the hole and illuminates all the Muppets. Joined by characters from other Henson productions – including _[Sesame Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesame\_Street "Sesame Street")_, _[Emmet Otter's Jug-Band Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmet\_Otter's\_Jug-Band\_Christmas "Emmet Otter's Jug-Band Christmas")_, and _[The Land of Gorch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Land\_of\_Gorch "The Land of Gorch")_ – the Muppets sing the final verse in a reprise of "Rainbow Connection". As the film ends, Sweetums tears through the screen, elated that he caught up with them.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Development")]

After the popularity of the Muppets had grown following the success of _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_, [Lew Grade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lew_Grade "Lew Grade") agreed to finance the production of the film and signed the deal with his company [ITC Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITC_Entertainment "ITC Entertainment"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199472-10) which helped Jim Henson finance the film.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-11) After the film's production greenlit, [Jim Henson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Henson "Jim Henson") and selected team members traveled to [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") various times to develop the script, music, and infrastructure in [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles") to shoot the film.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12)[James Frawley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Frawley "James Frawley") was hired to direct the movie due to the film's challenges.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12)

During Frawley and Henson's first meeting in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), they were concerned that the Muppets would not blend well in [real life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_life "Real life").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Frawley-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:5-14) Along with [Frank Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Oz "Frank Oz") and the team, they filmed and tested how the characters would appear in real-world locations during the first few days of June 1978 in a UK meadow.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Frawley-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:5-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:1-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473-16) During filming tests, a cow was ambled near Fozzie for an unexpected rear look at a comparison between fake and natural fur hair.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473-16) The camera tests attracted the investment of [ITC Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITC_Entertainment "ITC Entertainment").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12) On July 3, 1978, Henson flew to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") again to begin shooting for the film.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:1-15)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Filming")]

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began on July 5, 1978, and continued for 87 days during summer and fall of that year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJay_Jones2013283-17) Each minute took a day to be filmed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9) Filming locations included [Albuquerque, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico") as well as various parts of Los Angeles and [Northern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_California "Northern California"), including the [San Fernando Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Valley "San Fernando Valley").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Frawley-13)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-NMex-18) The Western street scenes were filmed on the former Columbia Ranch, then known as The Burbank Studios.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-19) Additionally, the interior shots were filmed at [CBS-MTM Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radford_Studio_Center "Radford Studio Center").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12) All the sets were elevated by five feet to allow the puppeteers to perform.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:0-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-21) According to Henson, the principal photography of the film was slower than in television.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:0-20) No effects were added after filming concluded.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Frawley-13)

[Austin Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Pendleton "Austin Pendleton") recalled that the film was shot on "a very unhappy set, because Jim [Frawley] was very unhappy directing that movie. And I noticed that was the only time the Muppet people used an outside person to direct a Muppet movie. They never did that again. After that, it was either Jim Henson or Frank Oz. And I would have liked to have been in one of those, because those sets were very harmonious. But this was not."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-22)

Several shots required Muppets standing and acting in a full-body shot. To perform Kermit sitting on a log, Henson squeezed into a specially designed metal container complete with an air hose (to breathe), a rubber sleeve which came out of the top to perform Kermit and a monitor to see his performance, and placed himself under the water, log, and the Kermit puppet.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473-16)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-23) He was also assisted in this operation by [Kathryn Mullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathryn_Mullen "Kathryn Mullen") and [Steve Whitmire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Whitmire "Steve Whitmire").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-24) During breaks, cups of ice tea were given to Henson through the rubber sleeve since he could not easily leave the tank.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473-16) Rescuers had to stand by the tank to pull Henson out if the tank leaked or the air supply had difficulties.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473-16) The scene took five days to be filmed.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJay_Jones2013235-25)

In order for Kermit to ride a bicycle in a full-body shot, a Kermit puppet with legs was posed onto the seat and his legs and arms were attached to the pedals and handlebars. An overhead crane with a marionette system held the bicycle through strong strings invisible to the camera, guiding the bicycle forward.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-26) The crane and system were out of the camera's frame of vision.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Frawley-13) Specially made, remote-controlled puppets were placed on the set and controlled by puppeteers out of the frame. A dancing Kermit and [Fozzie Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fozzie_Bear "Fozzie Bear") were operated by Henson and Oz in front of a [blue screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chroma_key "Chroma key"), and they were composited onto a separate reel of the stage.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] For scenes involving Fozzie driving a [Studebaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker_Champion "Studebaker Champion"), cables, TV monitors, puppeteers, and its Muppets were filled in.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473%E2%80%9374-27) A [dwarf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwarfism "Dwarfism") would sit in the trunk and control via remote control. A television monitor showed what was ahead.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199474-28)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9)

The closing reprise of "Rainbow Connection" featured a crowd of more than 250 Muppet characters—virtually every Muppet that had been created up to that point in time.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:5-14)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:3-29) According to Henson Archivist Karen Falk, 137 puppeteers were enlisted from the Puppeteers of America (along with the regular Muppets performers) to perform every Muppet extant.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:3-29) Prior to the day-long filming of the shot, Henson gave the enthusiastic participants a lesson in the art of cinematic puppetry. The scene involved 150 puppeteers performing in a pit that was 6 feet (1.8 m) deep and 17 feet (5.2 m) wide.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:3-29) In September 1978, [Edgar Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen "Edgar Bergen"), Henson's idol who appeared in a cameo role, died shortly after completing his scenes. Henson was asked by his family to say a few words with Kermit for his memorial service. Henson agreed, and he attended Bergen's memorial service for its speech.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199475-30) Henson dedicated the film to his memory.

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Music")]

Main article: [_The Muppet Movie_ (soundtrack)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie_(soundtrack) "The Muppet Movie (soundtrack)")

The film's music and lyrics were written by [Paul Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Williams_(songwriter) "Paul Williams (songwriter)") and [Kenneth Ascher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Ascher "Kenneth Ascher"). Regarding the music's composition, Williams said; "Jim Henson gave you more [creative] freedom than anybody I've ever worked with in my life. I said, 'You want to hear the songs as we're writing them?' He said, 'No. I'll hear them in the studio. I know I'm gonna love them.' You just don't get that kind of freedom on a project these days."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-songfacts-31) "Never Before, Never Again" was originally sung by [Johnny Mathis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Mathis "Johnny Mathis"), but was changed to Miss Piggy when Jim Henson thought it would be funnier if she sang it to herself.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:3-29) Mathis would later sing the song in the television special _[The Muppets Go Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppets\_Go\_Hollywood "The Muppets Go Hollywood")_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:3-29)

"Movin' Right Along", "Never Before, Never Again", and "I Hope That Somethin' Better Comes Along" were shortened in the film, compared to their soundtrack versions, for continuity purposes.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The latter, a duet between Rowlf and Kermit, contained references that the studio considered too mature for children, although the song appeared complete in the British theatrical and home video debut versions.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Marketing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Marketing")]

In May 1979, [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") aired _[The Muppets Go Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppets\_Go\_Hollywood "The Muppets Go Hollywood")_, a one-hour television special that promoted the then-upcoming release of _The Muppet Movie_. In April, the film had been promoted when the Muppets hosted _[The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show\_Starring\_Johnny\_Carson "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson")_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJay_Jones2013291-42) Additionally, a book adaptation of _The Muppet Movie_, adapted by Steven Crist, was published by Peacock Press/[Bantam Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantam_Books "Bantam Books").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-43)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-44)

In [Austin, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas "Austin, Texas"), then-CBS affiliate [KTBC-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KTBC-TV "KTBC-TV") and American International Traveler sponsored a contest where adults who paid to see the film in the area were eligible to win a free trip to [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Muppet_Movie_Austin-37)

### Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Home media")]

_The Muppet Movie_ was the first film by [ITC Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITC_Films "ITC Films") to be released on [home video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_video "Home video") when [Magnetic Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_Video "Magnetic Video") issued it in May 1980, having acquired the video rights to ITC's films. It was reissued in 1982 and 1984 by [CBS/Fox Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS/Fox_Video "CBS/Fox Video"). On January 29, 1993, [Buena Vista Home Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buena_Vista_Home_Video "Buena Vista Home Video") re-released the film under their [Jim Henson Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Henson_Video "Jim Henson Video") label on VHS and [LaserDisc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaserDisc "LaserDisc"), pricing at $24.99.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-45)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-46)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-47) The movie was reissued again on VHS by [Columbia TriStar Home Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_TriStar_Home_Video "Columbia TriStar Home Video") and Jim Henson Home Entertainment on June 1, 1999, followed by a DVD release on June 5, 2001.

After [The Walt Disney Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company")'s acquisition of the Muppets in 2004, the film rights to _The Muppet Movie_ were acquired by Disney; the film was reissued under the [Walt Disney Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures") banner in home media formats and was re-released by [Buena Vista Home Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buena_Vista_Home_Entertainment "Buena Vista Home Entertainment") on DVD on November 29, 2005, as part of the _Kermit's 50th Anniversary Edition_ line. Disney released the film as the _Nearly 35th Anniversary Edition_ on [Blu-ray Disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray_Disc "Blu-ray Disc") and DVD on August 13, 2013. The film now streams in [4K Ultra HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4K_Ultra_HD "4K Ultra HD") on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-48)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Box office")]

In its first six days at the Leicester Square Theatre, it grossed $31,884.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-49) The film would later earn over $65 million in the United States and Canada,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJay_Jones2013296-7) returning $32 million in box office rentals.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-50)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-51) For 32 years, _The Muppet Movie_ was the [highest-grossing puppet film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_puppet_films "List of highest-grossing puppet films") until the release of _[The Muppets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppets\_(2011\_film) "The Muppets (2011 film)")_ in 2011.

The film's successful theatrical release encouraged [Lew Grade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lew_Grade "Lew Grade") into furthering his own film distribution company, which later backfired with the massive box office failures of _[Can't Stop the Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't\_Stop\_the\_Music "Can't Stop the Music")_ (from [EMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMI_Films "EMI Films")) and _[Raise the Titanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raise\_the\_Titanic\_(film) "Raise the Titanic (film)")_ (from [ITC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITC_Films "ITC Films")), both released by [Associated Film Distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Film_Distribution "Associated Film Distribution") just a year later.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-grade-52)

### Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

_The Muppet Movie_ currently holds an 89% approval rating on [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), based on 102 reviews. The site's consensus says "_The Muppet Movie_, the big-screen debut of Jim Henson's plush creations, is smart, lighthearted, and fun for all ages."[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-RT-53) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film has a weighted average score of 74 out of 100 based on 7 reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-54)

The film received highly positive reviews in the United States. [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") of the _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_ gave the film three-and-a-half out of four stars. In his favorable review, he was fascinated that "_The Muppet Movie_ not only stars the Muppets but, for the first time, shows us their feet."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-ebert-55)[Vincent Canby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Canby "Vincent Canby") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ offered equal praise, stating that the film "demonstrates once again that there's always room in movies for unbridled amiability when it is governed by intelligence and wit."[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-56)[Gene Siskel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Siskel "Gene Siskel") of the _[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")_ gave the film three-and-a-half stars out of four and called it "surely one of the summer's most entertaining films," which "does a fairly nice job of trying to be all things to all people. Which is not an easy job."[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-57)[Dale Pollock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dale_Pollock "Dale Pollock") of _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ wrote, "'The Muppet Movie' is a winner... Script by Jerry Juhl and Jack Burns incorporates the zingy one-liners and bad puns that have become the teleseries' trade mark, but also develops the Muppets themselves as thinking, feeling characters."[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-58) Kathleen Carroll of the _[New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_Daily\_News "New York Daily News")_ wrote that "with the exception of Brooks' wacky scene and Steve Martin's funny bit as a snooty waiter, the cameo appearances by such stars as Bob Hope and Richard Pryor tend to slow the action down just as the bland musical numbers by Paul Williams and Kenny Asher interrupt the flow of the movie. Still _The Muppet Movie_ should entrance both young and old as the Muppets further endear themselves with their crazy antics, their playful puns and their very human characteristics."[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-59)[Rex Reed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Reed "Rex Reed"), in the same newspaper, reacted more enthusiastically to the film, remarking that "if there's any doubt, _The Muppet Movie_ will make believers and fans out of the worst pessimists. These lovable characters are so real and so endearing that I was never aware of the human hands making them work from mysterious hiding places. The Muppets made a wide-eyed, child out of me, and I hope they continue to do so until I'm in my wheelchair."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-60)

[Charles Champlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Champlin "Charles Champlin") of the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ wrote, "as you might well expect, it is hip, funny, technically ingenious, fast-moving, melodious, richly produced, contemporary and equally and utterly beguiling to grown-ups and small persons."[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-61) Katrine Ames of _[Newsweek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsweek "Newsweek")_ stated, "'The Muppet Movie' is a delectable grab bag of influences — stories by [L. Frank Baum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L._Frank_Baum "L. Frank Baum") and [Lewis Carroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Carroll "Lewis Carroll"), Westerns, the [Crosby-Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_to_... "Road to ...") and [Garland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Garland "Judy Garland")-[Rooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Rooney "Mickey Rooney") movies — as well as its own inventive devices. The result is a kind of '[That's Entertainment!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's_Entertainment! "That's Entertainment!")' with a plot attached. Its charm — and success — lie primarily in its loving pokes at Hollywood conventions and in the lovable characters who do the poking."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-62) John Skow of _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ magazine offered a more mixed response, saying that "the transition from the yank-'em-off-if-they-bomb lunacy of the TV show to the coherent narration of the film is not a complete success. Muppet magic remains a bewildering succession of wonderful bits, and perhaps the movie's best occurs when Rowlf the Dog, who is a barroom pianist, commiserates with Kermit, who has just been deserted by Miss Piggy. The two sing a nice, rueful song about women—the can't-live-with-them, can't-live-without-them kind of thing."[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-63)

Michael Hanton of the _[Toronto Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto\_Star "Toronto Star")_ wrote that "I was looking forward to a combination of _[Singin' in the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singin'\_in\_the\_Rain "Singin' in the Rain")_, _[Citizen Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizen\_Kane "Citizen Kane")_, and _[Intolerance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intolerance\_(film) "Intolerance (film)")_. What I got was more like _[Gidget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gidget "Gidget")_, _[The Great Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Race "The Great Race")_ and _[Love Boat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Boat "Love Boat")_"; he also remarked that Fozzie Bear stole the show from his favorite character, Miss Piggy.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-64)

In the United Kingdom, it received mixed to positive reviews. Tim Radford of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ called it "another film spun slightly longer than it should have been", adding that "the humour remains decently dry and self-deprecating throughout; on the other hand there isn't nearly enough of it, and a good 40 or 50 minute idea is padded to the obligatory hour and a half with songs, travelogue, flashbacks and a certain amount of mooning about."[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-65) Patrick Gibbs of _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ remarked that "after [the Wombles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wombles "The Wombles") moved, as they did recently, from [the small screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wombles_(1973_TV_series) "The Wombles (1973 TV series)") to [the big](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wombling_Free "Wombling Free"), so the Muppets inevitably follow, rather more successfully, I think, for James Frawley’s _The Muppet Movie_ is a clever construction." He also said that "the style is cunningly varied at intervals by the appearance in virtually two-line parts of such people as Milton Berle, James Coburn, Dom DeLuise or Elliott Gould, not to mention Orson Welles, each in his own comic persona. Songs also help to add variety to a very hazardous undertaking; not at all to my taste, it comes off, I would say, as well as possible."[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-66)[Alexander Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Walker_(critic) "Alexander Walker (critic)") of the _[London Evening Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London\_Evening\_Standard "London Evening Standard")_ supplied the film with its most positive review in the country, calling it "the most original little show in town", and adding that it offered:

> Across the board delight: not only for the children: for adults, too, who'll relish its in-jokes, visual wit, cheeky parodies of other movies and [its] own brand of surrealist fun.
> 
> 
> That's the first surprise. The second is how successfully the Muppets take to the big blow-up of the cinema screen. But this is no jumped-up clone of the TV show. It expands its own fun to fill its enlarged running-time.
> 
> 
> It reminds you of a "Road" film. But instead of Hope, [Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby") and [Lamour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Lamour "Dorothy Lamour"), it has a cloth-and-styrofoam cast who look more human than the famous humanoids like Orson Welles, Mel Brooks, Telly Savalas and (yes) Bob Hope they meet en route.
> 
> 
> The Muppets "magic," supplied by creator-producer Jim Henson and other talented artists operating the globe puppets from hiding places that a sewer rat would think cramped, endow their stars with independent life and liveliness.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-67)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Legacy")]

In 2009, it was selected for preservation in the [National Film Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Registry "National Film Registry") by the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress") for being "culturally, historically or aesthetically significant."[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:4-76) In 2020, "Rainbow Connection" was deemed "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant" by the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress") and selected for preservation in the [National Recording Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Recording_Registry "National Recording Registry").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-77) One of the two 1951 Studebaker Commander 2-door sedans used in the film is now on display at the [Studebaker National Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker_National_Museum "Studebaker National Museum") in [South Bend, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana "South Bend, Indiana"). The car was used for the driving scenes. The bottom of the front seat was removed, and the puppeteers lay on the floor to move the muppets. The car was driven by an operator seated in the trunk using remote controls. A camera hidden in the "bullet" at the front of the car provided a closed-circuit video feed to a monitor in the trunk for the operator. In July 2025 the car completed an 18-month restoration. [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

_**The Muppet Movie**_ is a 1979 [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_film "Musical film")[road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_movie "Road movie")[comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film"), directed by [James Frawley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Frawley "James Frawley") and produced by [Jim Henson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Henson "Jim Henson"), and the first theatrical film to feature [the Muppets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppets "The Muppets"). A co-production between the United Kingdom and the United States, the film was written by _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_ writers [Jerry Juhl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Juhl "Jerry Juhl") and [Jack Burns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Burns "Jack Burns"). Produced during the third season of _The Muppet Show_, the film tells the [origin story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origin_story "Origin story") of the Muppets, as [Kermit the Frog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kermit_the_Frog "Kermit the Frog") embarks on a cross-country trip to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), encountering several of the Muppets—who all share the same ambition of finding success in professional show business—along the way while being pursued by Doc Hopper, a greedy [restaurateur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restaurateur "Restaurateur") with intentions of recruiting Kermit to promote his [frog legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frog_legs "Frog legs") business.

The film stars Muppet performers Henson, [Frank Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Oz "Frank Oz"), [Jerry Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Nelson "Jerry Nelson"), [Richard Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Hunt_(puppeteer) "Richard Hunt (puppeteer)"), and [Dave Goelz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Goelz "Dave Goelz"), as well as [Charles Durning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Durning "Charles Durning") and [Austin Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Pendleton "Austin Pendleton"), and it features cameo appearances by [Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope "Bob Hope"), [Dom DeLuise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dom_DeLuise "Dom DeLuise"), [James Coburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Coburn "James Coburn"), [Cloris Leachman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloris_Leachman "Cloris Leachman"), [Richard Pryor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor "Richard Pryor"), [Telly Savalas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telly_Savalas "Telly Savalas"), [Edgar Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen "Edgar Bergen") (in his final film appearance before his death), [Orson Welles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orson_Welles "Orson Welles"), [Madeline Kahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madeline_Kahn "Madeline Kahn"), [Milton Berle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Berle "Milton Berle"), [Carol Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_Kane "Carol Kane"), [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin"), [Mel Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Brooks "Mel Brooks"), [Elliott Gould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliott_Gould "Elliott Gould"), and [Paul Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Williams_(songwriter) "Paul Williams (songwriter)"). Notable for its [surreal humour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surreal_humour "Surreal humour"), [meta-references](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta-reference "Meta-reference") and prolific use of [cameos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_appearance "Cameo appearance"), _The Muppet Movie_ was distributed by [Associated Film Distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Film_Distribution "Associated Film Distribution") in the United Kingdom on May 31, 1979, and in the United States on June 22, 1979.

The film received critical praise, including two [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") nominations for [Paul Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Williams_(songwriter) "Paul Williams (songwriter)") and [Kenneth Ascher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Ascher "Kenneth Ascher")'s [musical score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score") and their song "[Rainbow Connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow_Connection "Rainbow Connection")". The film grossed $65.2 million worldwide against an $8 million budget. _The Muppet Movie_ was followed by seven feature films starring the Muppets as well as several more television series and media. In 2009, the film was deemed "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant" by the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress") and selected for preservation in the [National Film Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Registry "National Film Registry").

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

The story opens with [the Muppets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppets "The Muppets") sitting down for a private screening of a movie that acts as an origin story of how they all met.

[Kermit the Frog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kermit_the_Frog "Kermit the Frog") lives a simple life in a [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida") swamp. After he plays [his banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Banjo_Museum#Jim_Henson "American Banjo Museum") and sings "[Rainbow Connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow_Connection "Rainbow Connection")", he is approached by Bernie, a [talent agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_agent "Talent agent") who encourages him to pursue a career in show business. Inspired, Kermit sets off on a cross-country trip to [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles").

He meets [Fozzie Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fozzie_Bear "Fozzie Bear"), who is working as a hapless [stand-up comedian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stand-up_comedy "Stand-up comedy"), and invites him on his journey. The two set out in Fozzie's 1951 [Studebaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker_Champion "Studebaker Champion") but are pursued by entrepreneur Doc Hopper and his assistant Max, who try to convince Kermit to be the new spokesfrog of Hopper's struggling [French-fried](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_frying "Deep frying")[frog legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frog_legs "Frog legs") restaurant franchise. Horrified, Kermit refuses, and he and Fozzie drive away. Unwilling to accept Kermit's refusal, Hopper follows the pair and resorts to increasingly forceful means of persuasion. In an old church, Kermit and Fozzie meet the rock band [Dr. Teeth and the Electric Mayhem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Teeth_and_the_Electric_Mayhem "Dr. Teeth and the Electric Mayhem"), and their manager [Scooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scooter_(Muppet) "Scooter (Muppet)"), who help them disguise their car. Driving on, they meet and are joined by [Gonzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonzo_(Muppet) "Gonzo (Muppet)") and his girlfriend [Camilla the Chicken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camilla_the_Chicken "Camilla the Chicken"), who are also interested in becoming movie stars. They trade in their failing vehicle at a used car lot, where they meet [Sweetums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweetums "Sweetums"). They invite Sweetums to come with them, but he runs away. The others drive away, only for Sweetums to emerge and reveal that he had only gone to pack his things.

The group meets [Miss Piggy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_Piggy "Miss Piggy") at a county fair and she and Kermit become love-stricken with each other. When they meet for dinner that night, Hopper and Max abduct Miss Piggy as bait to lure Kermit. When they capture Kermit, Hopper orders mad scientist Professor Krassman to give Kermit an electric lobotomy so that he would willingly perform in Hopper's advertisements, but Miss Piggy knocks out Hopper's henchmen and causes Krassman to have his brain fried by his own device. Immediately after the fight, however, Miss Piggy receives a job offer and abandons a devastated Kermit.

Joined by [Rowlf the Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rowlf_the_Dog "Rowlf the Dog"), the Muppets pick up Miss Piggy – who is hitchhiking on the side of the road – and continue their journey; but their car breaks down in the desert. Sitting at a campfire, the group realizes that they will likely miss the auditions the next day. Kermit wanders off, ashamed for bringing his friends on a fruitless journey, but [personal reflection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_monologue "Internal monologue") restores his commitment. He returns to camp, where he discovers that the Electric Mayhem have come to their rescue, [having learned of their plight by reading ahead in the film's script](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_wall "Fourth wall"). The Mayhem offer to drive the group the rest of the way in their bus.

The group is warned by a reformed Max that Hopper has hired an assassin, Snake Walker, to kill Kermit. Kermit decides to face his aggressor and proposes a Western-style showdown in a nearby [ghost town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_town "Ghost town"). There, they find inventor [Dr. Bunsen Honeydew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Bunsen_Honeydew "Dr. Bunsen Honeydew") and his assistant [Beaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaker_(Muppet) "Beaker (Muppet)"). Kermit and his friends are saved when one of Dr. Honeydew's inventions, "insta-grow" pills, enlarges Mayhem drummer [Animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_(Muppet) "Animal (Muppet)"), who frightens away Hopper and his henchmen.

Once the Muppets reach the Hollywood studio, they meet executive Lew Lord, who signs them to a "standard 'rich and famous' contract". The first take in their attempt to perform the script goes awry when Gonzo crashes into the prop rainbow, which knocks the scenery down and an explosion blows a hole in the roof of the studio, but a real rainbow shines through the hole and illuminates all the Muppets. Joined by characters from other Henson productions – including _[Sesame Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesame\_Street "Sesame Street")_, _[Emmet Otter's Jug-Band Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmet\_Otter's\_Jug-Band\_Christmas "Emmet Otter's Jug-Band Christmas")_, and _[The Land of Gorch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Land\_of\_Gorch "The Land of Gorch")_ – the Muppets sing the final verse in a reprise of "Rainbow Connection". As the film ends, Sweetums tears through the screen, elated that he caught up with them.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Development")]

After the popularity of the Muppets had grown following the success of _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_, [Lew Grade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lew_Grade "Lew Grade") agreed to finance the production of the film and signed the deal with his company [ITC Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITC_Entertainment "ITC Entertainment"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199472-10) which helped Jim Henson finance the film.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-11) After the film's production greenlit, [Jim Henson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Henson "Jim Henson") and selected team members traveled to [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") various times to develop the script, music, and infrastructure in [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles") to shoot the film.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12)[James Frawley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Frawley "James Frawley") was hired to direct the movie due to the film's challenges.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12)

During Frawley and Henson's first meeting in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), they were concerned that the Muppets would not blend well in [real life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_life "Real life").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Frawley-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:5-14) Along with [Frank Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Oz "Frank Oz") and the team, they filmed and tested how the characters would appear in real-world locations during the first few days of June 1978 in a UK meadow.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Frawley-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:5-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:1-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473-16) During filming tests, a cow was ambled near Fozzie for an unexpected rear look at a comparison between fake and natural fur hair.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473-16) The camera tests attracted the investment of [ITC Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITC_Entertainment "ITC Entertainment").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12) On July 3, 1978, Henson flew to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") again to begin shooting for the film.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:1-15)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Filming")]

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began on July 5, 1978, and continued for 87 days during summer and fall of that year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJay_Jones2013283-17) Each minute took a day to be filmed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9) Filming locations included [Albuquerque, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico") as well as various parts of Los Angeles and [Northern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_California "Northern California"), including the [San Fernando Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Valley "San Fernando Valley").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Frawley-13)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-NMex-18) The Western street scenes were filmed on the former Columbia Ranch, then known as The Burbank Studios.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-19) Additionally, the interior shots were filmed at [CBS-MTM Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radford_Studio_Center "Radford Studio Center").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:6-12) All the sets were elevated by five feet to allow the puppeteers to perform.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:0-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-21) According to Henson, the principal photography of the film was slower than in television.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:0-20) No effects were added after filming concluded.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Frawley-13)

[Austin Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Pendleton "Austin Pendleton") recalled that the film was shot on "a very unhappy set, because Jim [Frawley] was very unhappy directing that movie. And I noticed that was the only time the Muppet people used an outside person to direct a Muppet movie. They never did that again. After that, it was either Jim Henson or Frank Oz. And I would have liked to have been in one of those, because those sets were very harmonious. But this was not."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-22)

Several shots required Muppets standing and acting in a full-body shot. To perform Kermit sitting on a log, Henson squeezed into a specially designed metal container complete with an air hose (to breathe), a rubber sleeve which came out of the top to perform Kermit and a monitor to see his performance, and placed himself under the water, log, and the Kermit puppet.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473-16)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-23) He was also assisted in this operation by [Kathryn Mullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathryn_Mullen "Kathryn Mullen") and [Steve Whitmire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Whitmire "Steve Whitmire").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-24) During breaks, cups of ice tea were given to Henson through the rubber sleeve since he could not easily leave the tank.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473-16) Rescuers had to stand by the tank to pull Henson out if the tank leaked or the air supply had difficulties.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473-16) The scene took five days to be filmed.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJay_Jones2013235-25)

In order for Kermit to ride a bicycle in a full-body shot, a Kermit puppet with legs was posed onto the seat and his legs and arms were attached to the pedals and handlebars. An overhead crane with a marionette system held the bicycle through strong strings invisible to the camera, guiding the bicycle forward.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-26) The crane and system were out of the camera's frame of vision.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Frawley-13) Specially made, remote-controlled puppets were placed on the set and controlled by puppeteers out of the frame. A dancing Kermit and [Fozzie Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fozzie_Bear "Fozzie Bear") were operated by Henson and Oz in front of a [blue screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chroma_key "Chroma key"), and they were composited onto a separate reel of the stage.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] For scenes involving Fozzie driving a [Studebaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker_Champion "Studebaker Champion"), cables, TV monitors, puppeteers, and its Muppets were filled in.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199473%E2%80%9374-27) A [dwarf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwarfism "Dwarfism") would sit in the trunk and control via remote control. A television monitor showed what was ahead.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199474-28)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9)

The closing reprise of "Rainbow Connection" featured a crowd of more than 250 Muppet characters—virtually every Muppet that had been created up to that point in time.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:5-14)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:3-29) According to Henson Archivist Karen Falk, 137 puppeteers were enlisted from the Puppeteers of America (along with the regular Muppets performers) to perform every Muppet extant.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:3-29) Prior to the day-long filming of the shot, Henson gave the enthusiastic participants a lesson in the art of cinematic puppetry. The scene involved 150 puppeteers performing in a pit that was 6 feet (1.8 m) deep and 17 feet (5.2 m) wide.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:22-9)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:3-29) In September 1978, [Edgar Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen "Edgar Bergen"), Henson's idol who appeared in a cameo role, died shortly after completing his scenes. Henson was asked by his family to say a few words with Kermit for his memorial service. Henson agreed, and he attended Bergen's memorial service for its speech.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurrett199475-30) Henson dedicated the film to his memory.

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Music")]

Main article: [_The Muppet Movie_ (soundtrack)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie_(soundtrack) "The Muppet Movie (soundtrack)")

The film's music and lyrics were written by [Paul Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Williams_(songwriter) "Paul Williams (songwriter)") and [Kenneth Ascher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Ascher "Kenneth Ascher"). Regarding the music's composition, Williams said; "Jim Henson gave you more [creative] freedom than anybody I've ever worked with in my life. I said, 'You want to hear the songs as we're writing them?' He said, 'No. I'll hear them in the studio. I know I'm gonna love them.' You just don't get that kind of freedom on a project these days."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-songfacts-31) "Never Before, Never Again" was originally sung by [Johnny Mathis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Mathis "Johnny Mathis"), but was changed to Miss Piggy when Jim Henson thought it would be funnier if she sang it to herself.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:3-29) Mathis would later sing the song in the television special _[The Muppets Go Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppets\_Go\_Hollywood "The Muppets Go Hollywood")_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-:3-29)

"Movin' Right Along", "Never Before, Never Again", and "I Hope That Somethin' Better Comes Along" were shortened in the film, compared to their soundtrack versions, for continuity purposes.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The latter, a duet between Rowlf and Kermit, contained references that the studio considered too mature for children, although the song appeared complete in the British theatrical and home video debut versions.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Marketing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Marketing")]

In May 1979, [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") aired _[The Muppets Go Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppets\_Go\_Hollywood "The Muppets Go Hollywood")_, a one-hour television special that promoted the then-upcoming release of _The Muppet Movie_. In April, the film had been promoted when the Muppets hosted _[The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show\_Starring\_Johnny\_Carson "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson")_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJay_Jones2013291-42) Additionally, a book adaptation of _The Muppet Movie_, adapted by Steven Crist, was published by Peacock Press/[Bantam Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantam_Books "Bantam Books").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-43)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-44)

In [Austin, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas "Austin, Texas"), then-CBS affiliate [KTBC-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KTBC-TV "KTBC-TV") and American International Traveler sponsored a contest where adults who paid to see the film in the area were eligible to win a free trip to [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-Muppet_Movie_Austin-37)

### Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Home media")]

_The Muppet Movie_ was the first film by [ITC Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITC_Films "ITC Films") to be released on [home video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_video "Home video") when [Magnetic Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_Video "Magnetic Video") issued it in May 1980, having acquired the video rights to ITC's films. It was reissued in 1982 and 1984 by [CBS/Fox Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS/Fox_Video "CBS/Fox Video"). On January 29, 1993, [Buena Vista Home Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buena_Vista_Home_Video "Buena Vista Home Video") re-released the film under their [Jim Henson Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Henson_Video "Jim Henson Video") label on VHS and [LaserDisc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaserDisc "LaserDisc"), pricing at $24.99.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-45)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-46)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-47) The movie was reissued again on VHS by [Columbia TriStar Home Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_TriStar_Home_Video "Columbia TriStar Home Video") and Jim Henson Home Entertainment on June 1, 1999, followed by a DVD release on June 5, 2001.

After [The Walt Disney Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company")'s acquisition of the Muppets in 2004, the film rights to _The Muppet Movie_ were acquired by Disney; the film was reissued under the [Walt Disney Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures") banner in home media formats and was re-released by [Buena Vista Home Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buena_Vista_Home_Entertainment "Buena Vista Home Entertainment") on DVD on November 29, 2005, as part of the _Kermit's 50th Anniversary Edition_ line. Disney released the film as the _Nearly 35th Anniversary Edition_ on [Blu-ray Disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray_Disc "Blu-ray Disc") and DVD on August 13, 2013. The film now streams in [4K Ultra HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4K_Ultra_HD "4K Ultra HD") on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-48)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Box office")]

In its first six days at the Leicester Square Theatre, it grossed $31,884.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-49) The film would later earn over $65 million in the United States and Canada,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJay_Jones2013296-7) returning $32 million in box office rentals.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-50)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-51) For 32 years, _The Muppet Movie_ was the [highest-grossing puppet film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_puppet_films "List of highest-grossing puppet films") until the release of _[The Muppets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppets\_(2011\_film) "The Muppets (2011 film)")_ in 2011.

The film's successful theatrical release encouraged [Lew Grade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lew_Grade "Lew Grade") into furthering his own film distribution company, which later backfired with the massive box office failures of _[Can't Stop the Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't\_Stop\_the\_Music "Can't Stop the Music")_ (from [EMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMI_Films "EMI Films")) and _[Raise the Titanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raise\_the\_Titanic\_(film) "Raise the Titanic (film)")_ (from [ITC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITC_Films "ITC Films")), both released by [Associated Film Distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Film_Distribution "Associated Film Distribution") just a year later.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-grade-52)

### Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Muppet_Movie&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

_The Muppet Movie_ currently holds an 89% approval rating on [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), based on 102 reviews. The site's consensus says "_The Muppet Movie_, the big-screen debut of Jim Henson's plush creations, is smart, lighthearted, and fun for all ages."[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-RT-53) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film has a weighted average score of 74 out of 100 based on 7 reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-54)

The film received highly positive reviews in the United States. [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") of the _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_ gave the film three-and-a-half out of four stars. In his favorable review, he was fascinated that "_The Muppet Movie_ not only stars the Muppets but, for the first time, shows us their feet."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-ebert-55)[Vincent Canby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Canby "Vincent Canby") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ offered equal praise, stating that the film "demonstrates once again that there's always room in movies for unbridled amiability when it is governed by intelligence and wit."[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-56)[Gene Siskel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Siskel "Gene Siskel") of the _[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")_ gave the film three-and-a-half stars out of four and called it "surely one of the summer's most entertaining films," which "does a fairly nice job of trying to be all things to all people. Which is not an easy job."[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-57)[Dale Pollock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dale_Pollock "Dale Pollock") of _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ wrote, "'The Muppet Movie' is a winner... Script by Jerry Juhl and Jack Burns incorporates the zingy one-liners and bad puns that have become the teleseries' trade mark, but also develops the Muppets themselves as thinking, feeling characters."[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-58) Kathleen Carroll of the _[New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_Daily\_News "New York Daily News")_ wrote that "with the exception of Brooks' wacky scene and Steve Martin's funny bit as a snooty waiter, the cameo appearances by such stars as Bob Hope and Richard Pryor tend to slow the action down just as the bland musical numbers by Paul Williams and Kenny Asher interrupt the flow of the movie. Still _The Muppet Movie_ should entrance both young and old as the Muppets further endear themselves with their crazy antics, their playful puns and their very human characteristics."[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-59)[Rex Reed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Reed "Rex Reed"), in the same newspaper, reacted more enthusiastically to the film, remarking that "if there's any doubt, _The Muppet Movie_ will make believers and fans out of the worst pessimists. These lovable characters are so real and so endearing that I was never aware of the human hands making them work from mysterious hiding places. The Muppets made a wide-eyed, child out of me, and I hope they continue to do so until I'm in my wheelchair."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-60)

[Charles Champlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Champlin "Charles Champlin") of the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ wrote, "as you might well expect, it is hip, funny, technically ingenious, fast-moving, melodious, richly produced, contemporary and equally and utterly beguiling to grown-ups and small persons."[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-61) Katrine Ames of _[Newsweek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsweek "Newsweek")_ stated, "'The Muppet Movie' is a delectable grab bag of influences — stories by [L. Frank Baum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L._Frank_Baum "L. Frank Baum") and [Lewis Carroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Carroll "Lewis Carroll"), Westerns, the [Crosby-Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_to_... "Road to ...") and [Garland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Garland "Judy Garland")-[Rooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Rooney "Mickey Rooney") movies — as well as its own inventive devices. The result is a kind of '[That's Entertainment!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's_Entertainment! "That's Entertainment!")' with a plot attached. Its charm — and success — lie primarily in its loving pokes at Hollywood conventions and in the lovable characters who do the poking."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-62) John Skow of _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ magazine offered a more mixed response, saying that "the transition from the yank-'em-off-if-they-bomb lunacy of the TV show to the coherent narration of the film is not a complete success. Muppet magic remains a bewildering succession of wonderful bits, and perhaps the movie's best occurs when Rowlf the Dog, who is a barroom pianist, commiserates with Kermit, who has just been deserted by Miss Piggy. The two sing a nice, rueful song about women—the can't-live-with-them, can't-live-without-them kind of thing."[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-63)

Michael Hanton of the _[Toronto Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto\_Star "Toronto Star")_ wrote that "I was looking forward to a combination of _[Singin' in the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singin'\_in\_the\_Rain "Singin' in the Rain")_, _[Citizen Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizen\_Kane "Citizen Kane")_, and _[Intolerance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intolerance\_(film) "Intolerance (film)")_. What I got was more like _[Gidget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gidget "Gidget")_, _[The Great Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Race "The Great Race")_ and _[Love Boat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Boat "Love Boat")_"; he also remarked that Fozzie Bear stole the show from his favorite character, Miss Piggy.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-64)

In the United Kingdom, it received mixed to positive reviews. Tim Radford of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ called it "another film spun slightly longer than it should have been", adding that "the humour remains decently dry and self-deprecating throughout; on the other hand there isn't nearly enough of it, and a good 40 or 50 minute idea is padded to the obligatory hour and a half with songs, travelogue, flashbacks and a certain amount of mooning about."[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-65) Patrick Gibbs of _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ remarked that "after [the Wombles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wombles "The Wombles") moved, as they did recently, from [the small screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wombles_(1973_TV_series) "The Wombles (1973 TV series)") to [the big](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wombling_Free "Wombling Free"), so the Muppets inevitably follow, rather more successfully, I think, for James Frawley’s _The Muppet Movie_ is a clever construction." He also said that "the style is cunningly varied at intervals by the appearance in virtually two-line parts of such people as Milton Berle, James Coburn, Dom DeLuise or Elliott Gould, not to mention Orson Welles, each in his own comic persona. Songs also help to add variety to a very hazardous undertaking; not at all to my taste, it comes off, I would say, as well as possible."[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-66)[Alexander Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Walker_(critic) "Alexander Walker (critic)") of the _[London Evening Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London\_Evening\_Standard "London Evening Standard")_ supplied the film with its most positive review in the country, calling it "the most original little show in town", and adding that it offered:

> Across the board delight: not only for the children: for adults, too, who'll relish its in-jokes, visual wit, cheeky parodies of other movies and [its] own brand of surrealist fun.
> 
> 
> That's the first surprise. The second is how successfully the Muppets take to the big blow-up of the cinema screen. But this is no jumped-up clone of the TV show. It expands its own fun to fill its enlarged running-time.
> 
> 
> It reminds you of a "Road" film. But instead of Hope, [Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby") and [Lamour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Lamour "Dorothy Lamour"), it has a cloth-and-styrofoam cast who look more human than the famous humanoids like Orson Welles, Mel Brooks, Telly Savalas and (yes) Bob Hope they meet en route.
> 
> 
> The Muppets "magic," supplied by creator-producer Jim Henson and other talented artists operating the globe puppets from hiding places that a sewer rat would think cramped, endow their stars with independent life and liveliness.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muppet_Movie#cite_note-67)
