[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Bob_Hope_gets_plaque_on_Hill.jpg/250px-Bob_Hope_gets_plaque_on_Hill.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_gets_plaque_on_Hill.jpg)

Hope and his wife Dolores on [Capitol Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Hill "Capitol Hill") as he received an award in 1978

Hope was awarded more than 2,000 honors and awards, including 54 honorary university doctorates. In 1963 President [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") awarded him the [Congressional Gold Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Gold_Medal "Congressional Gold Medal") for service to his country.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002152%E2%80%93153-110) President [Lyndon Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_Johnson "Lyndon Johnson") bestowed the [Presidential Medal of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom "Presidential Medal of Freedom") in 1969 for his service to the armed forces through the [USO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USO "USO").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-usa-patriotism.com-111) In 1982 he received the S. Roger Horchow Award for Greatest Public Service by a Private Citizen, an honor given annually by [Jefferson Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Awards "Jefferson Awards").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Horchow_Award-112) He was presented with the [National Medal of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Medal_of_Arts "National Medal of Arts") in 1995[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-National_Medal_of_Arts-113) and received the [Ronald Reagan Freedom Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award "Ronald Reagan Freedom Award") in 1997.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Times_Union_1997-114) On June 10, 1980, he became the 64th—and only civilian—recipient of the United States Air Force [Order of the Sword](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Sword_(United_States) "Order of the Sword (United States)") which recognizes individuals who have made significant contributions to the enlisted corps.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Air_University-115)

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/Nancy_Reagan_presents_Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award_to_Bob_Hope.jpg/250px-Nancy_Reagan_presents_Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award_to_Bob_Hope.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nancy_Reagan_presents_Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award_to_Bob_Hope.jpg)

[Nancy Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan") prepares to present Hope (then aged 94) with the [Ronald Reagan Freedom Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award "Ronald Reagan Freedom Award"), July 1997

Several buildings and facilities were renamed for Hope, including the historic [Fox California Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Theater_(Stockton,_California)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Fox Theater (Stockton, California) (page does not exist)") in downtown [Stockton, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockton,_California "Stockton, California"),[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Mohawk_Group-116) and the [Bob Hope Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Airport "Bob Hope Airport") in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Daily_News_2010-117) There is a Bob Hope Gallery at the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-118) In memory of his mother, Avis Townes Hope, Bob and Dolores Hope gave the [Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_the_National_Shrine_of_the_Immaculate_Conception "Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception") in Washington, D.C., a chapel called the Chapel of [Our Lady of Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Hope "Our Lady of Hope").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-119)[USNS _Bob Hope_(T-AKR-300)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Bob_Hope "MV Bob Hope") of the U.S. [Military Sealift Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Sealift_Command "Military Sealift Command") was named for the performer in 1997. It is one of very few [U.S. naval ships that were named after living people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._military_vessels_named_after_living_Americans "List of U.S. military vessels named after living Americans").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FAS_2011-120) The Air Force named a [C-17 Globemaster III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-17_Globemaster_III "C-17 Globemaster III") transport aircraft the _Spirit of Bob Hope_.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Warplanes_Online_Community-121)

In 1965, he was awarded an honorary Doctor of Humane Letters (L.H.D.) degree from [Whittier College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whittier_College "Whittier College").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-122)

In 1978, Hope was invited to [dot the "i"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University_Marching_Band#Script_Ohio_and_dotting_the_%22i%22 "Ohio State University Marching Band") in the [Ohio State University Marching Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University_Marching_Band "Ohio State University Marching Band")'s "Script Ohio" formation, an honor only given to non-band members on 14 occasions from 1936 through 2016.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-123)[Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen") wrote and narrated a documentary honoring him, _My Favorite Comedian_, shown at [Lincoln Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Center "Lincoln Center").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-124) In Hope's hometown of Cleveland, the refurbished [Lorain-Carnegie Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorain-Carnegie_Bridge "Lorain-Carnegie Bridge") was renamed the Hope Memorial Bridge in 1983, though differing claims have been made as to whether the bridge honors Hope himself, his entire family, or his stonemason father who helped in the bridge's construction. Also, East 14th Street near [Playhouse Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playhouse_Square "Playhouse Square") in Cleveland's theater district was renamed Memory Lane-Bob Hope Way in 2003 in honor of the entertainer's 100th birthday.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-125)

In 1992, Hope was honored with the "Lombardi Award of Excellence" from the Vince Lombardi Cancer Foundation. The award was created to honor the football coach's legacy, and is awarded annually to an individual who exemplifies his spirit. He was also inducted into [Omicron Delta Kappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omicron_Delta_Kappa "Omicron Delta Kappa"), the National Leadership Honor Society, in 1992 at [Ferris State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferris_State_University "Ferris State University"). On May 28, 2003, President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") established the [Bob Hope American Patriot Award](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Executive%20Order%2013306 "s:Executive Order 13306").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-126)

*   [25th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/25th_Academy_Awards "25th Academy Awards") (1952): Honorary Award for his contribution to the laughter of the world, his service to the motion picture industry, and his devotion to the American premise
*   [32nd Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_Academy_Awards "32nd Academy Awards") (1959): [Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Hersholt_Humanitarian_Award "Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award")

### Marriage and relationships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Marriage and relationships")]

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/1942-08-02_Residence_of_Bob_Hope%2C_North_Hollywood%2C_California_A.jpg/250px-1942-08-02_Residence_of_Bob_Hope%2C_North_Hollywood%2C_California_A.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1942-08-02_Residence_of_Bob_Hope,_North_Hollywood,_California_A.jpg)

Residence of Bob Hope, North Hollywood, California

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Bob_Hope_and_family.jpg/250px-Bob_Hope_and_family.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_and_family.jpg)

The Hope family; Back, from left: Tony, Dolores, and Linda; Front, from left: Kelly, Bob, and Nora

Hope was briefly married to vaudeville partner Grace Louise Troxell (1912–1992), a secretary from Chicago, Illinois. They were married on January 25, 1933, in Erie, Pennsylvania.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199866-128) They divorced in November 1934.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Sheridan_2014-129)

The couple had shared headliner status with Joe Howard at the Palace Theatre in April 1931, performing "Keep Smiling" and the "Antics of 1931".[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-130) They worked together at the RKO Albee, performing the "Antics of 1933" along with Ann Gillens and Johnny Peters in June of that year.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-131) The following month, singer [Dolores Reade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_Reade "Dolores Reade") joined Hope's vaudeville troupe and was performing with him at Loew's Metropolitan Theater. She was described as a "former [Ziegfeld beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziegfeld_girl "Ziegfeld girl") and one of society's favorite nightclub entertainers, having appeared at many private social functions at New York, Palm Beach, and Southampton".[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-132)

His marriage to Reade was fraught with ambiguities. As [Richard Zoglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Zoglin "Richard Zoglin") wrote in his 2014 biography _Hope: Entertainer of the Century_,

> Bob and Dolores always claimed that they married in February 1934 in Erie, Pennsylvania. But at that time, he was secretly married to his vaudeville partner Louise Troxell, after three years together on and off. I found divorce papers for Bob and Louise dated November 1934, so either Bob Hope was a bigamist, or he lied about marrying Dolores in February that year. He had actually married Louise in January 1933 in Erie when they were traveling on the vaudeville circuit. When he claimed he had married Dolores in Erie he was miles away in New York, on Broadway. More intriguing, there is no record anywhere of his marriage to Dolores, if it happened. And there are no wedding photos, either. But he never forgot Louise and quietly sent her money in her later years.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Sheridan_2014-129)

Dolores had been one of Hope's co-stars on Broadway in _Roberta_. The couple adopted four children: Linda (in 1939), Anthony "Tony" (1940–2004),[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-133) Kelly (1946), and Eleanora "Nora" (1946).[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199886%E2%80%9387-134) Bob and Dolores were also the legal guardians of Tracey, the youngest daughter of famous New York City bar owner [Bernard "Toots" Shor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toots_Shor "Toots Shor") and his wife, Marion "Baby" Shor.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-135) In 1935, the couple lived in Manhattan. In 1937, they moved to 10346 Moorpark Street in the [Toluca Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toluca_Lake "Toluca Lake") neighborhood of Los Angeles, where they would reside until their respective deaths.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-136)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-137)

Hope had a reputation as a womanizer and continued to see other women throughout his marriage.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199882,_90-138) Zoglin wrote that Hope had several "affairs with chorus girls, beauty queens, singers and showbiz wannabes". Women who have claimed to have been romantically linked to Hope include [Barbara Payton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Payton "Barbara Payton"), [Marilyn Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Maxwell "Marilyn Maxwell"), and [Rosemarie Frankland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemarie_Frankland "Rosemarie Frankland").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd200665-139)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd200666,_67-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd2006311-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd2006313-142)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd2006313-142)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Arthur_Marx_1993-143)

### Politics and beliefs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Politics and beliefs")]

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg/250px-Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg)

From left to right: [Spiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiro_Agnew "Spiro Agnew") and [Judy Agnew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Agnew "Judy Agnew"), Bob and [Dolores Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_Hope "Dolores Hope"), [Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") and [Pat Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Nixon "Pat Nixon"), [Nancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan") and [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan") during a campaign stop for the [Nixon-Agnew ticket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon-Agnew_ticket "Nixon-Agnew ticket") in California, 1971

Hope had extensive relationships with US Presidents from [Franklin D. Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt "Franklin D. Roosevelt") to [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") and often made topical political jokes in his comedic material. He hosted the [White House Correspondents Dinner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Correspondents_Dinner "White House Correspondents Dinner") three times in 1944, 1953, and 1976.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-144)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-ford-146) Hope was supportive politically of [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") Presidents such as [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") and [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-147)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-148)

In an interview with Hope biographer [Richard Zoglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Zoglin "Richard Zoglin") on [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR") he stated that "Bob Hope was the establishment. Bob Hope was friends with [Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon "Nixon"). Bob Hope was speaking in favor of the [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War"). Bob Hope was expressing that kind of backward, suburban, [WASP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WASP "WASP") view of minorities, [homosexuals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuals "Homosexuals"), the [women's movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_movement "Women's movement")."[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-149) Hope's beliefs and attitudes on social issues are a part of the plot of the 2020 film _[Misbehaviour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misbehaviour\_(film) "Misbehaviour (film)")_, which follows the [Women's Liberation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_Liberation "Women's Liberation") protests at the [Miss World 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_World_1970 "Miss World 1970") competition that Hope hosted; [Greg Kinnear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kinnear "Greg Kinnear") plays Hope.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-150)

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/President_Ronald_Reagan_and_Nancy_Reagan_Talking_with_Bob_Hope_During_The_State_Dinner_for_Prime_Minister_Thatcher_at_The_White_House_-_DPLA_-_2db8a4b53ef061b70538102c33453b61.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Ronald_Reagan_and_Nancy_Reagan_Talking_with_Bob_Hope_During_The_State_Dinner_for_Prime_Minister_Thatcher_at_The_White_House_-_DPLA_-_2db8a4b53ef061b70538102c33453b61.jpg)

Hope (left) with [Nancy Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan") and President [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan") in 1981

After the shootings of president Ronald Reagan and [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II") in 1981, Hope advocated for [gun control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_control "Gun control"). Hope told [Tom Shales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Shales "Tom Shales") of _The Washington Post_, "I'm for gun registration. I don't think any jerk that's coked up or anything should be allowed to walk in a store and buy a gun and turn around and shoot 19 people, you know? ... And what the hell, hunters can have their guns, they're registered. I've got a gun in each house for a warning thing; that can be registered ... They gotta tell me what's wrong with having them registered. That's all I wanna hear."[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-151) When Hope shared these views during an [ABC Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_Radio "ABC News Radio") interview, he quickly realized the repercussions. Vice President [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush"), who was visiting [West Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Point "West Point") the same day Hope taped a special there, had declined to meet with him. Additionally, at a luncheon in Washington that same week, Hope had planned to sit with Nancy Reagan, but she canceled at the last minute.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-152)

Hope's views on the gay community also evolved. At the height of [Anita Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Bryant "Anita Bryant")'s campaign to reverse the progress of gay rights and anti-discrimination legislation in Florida in 1977, he, as well as many other comedians, ridiculed her in their routines, but also expressed his disagreement with Bryant: "We're all entitled to our own sexual habits [and] I believe what these people do behind closed doors is their business ... Most of us today are aware of Anita Bryant's stand [but] I still think jobs should be based on talent, not whether a person is homosexual or heterosexual."[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-153) However, Texaco and Chrysler, sponsors for many of his TV specials, asked him to refrain from making further jokes about the subject.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-154) In February 1986, he joined [Elizabeth Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Taylor "Elizabeth Taylor"), to cohost a benefit for [American Foundation for AIDS Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Foundation_for_AIDS_Research "American Foundation for AIDS Research") and the [Arizona AIDS Fund Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_AIDS_Fund_Trust?action=edit&redlink=1 "Arizona AIDS Fund Trust (page does not exist)") in [Scottsdale, AZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsdale,_AZ "Scottsdale, AZ").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-155) Though expressing these supportive views, he occasionally used epithets and told jokes at the expense of the community yet showed remorse when called on it. During a performance at [Liberty Weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Weekend "Liberty Weekend") in 1986, Hope remarked, "I just heard that the [Statue of Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty "Statue of Liberty") has AIDS, but she doesn't know if she got it from the mouth of the [Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_River "Hudson River") or the [Staten Island Ferry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island_Ferry "Staten Island Ferry")."[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-156) Two months later, Hope took responsibility for telling the joke and apologized, explaining that he overheard the joke and thought it was funny.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-157) When Hope used the word "[fag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faggot "Faggot")" on a 1988 _[Tonight Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show\_Starring\_Johnny\_Carson "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson")_ appearance, [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD "GLAAD") asked for a statement apologizing for the slur. He agreed to tape a public service announcement opposing "bigotry" on their behalf.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-158)

### Philanthropy and estate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Philanthropy and estate")]

Hope, who suffered from vision problems for much of his adult life, served as an active honorary chairman on the board of [Fight for Sight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fight_for_Sight_(U.S.) "Fight for Sight (U.S.)"), a nonprofit organization in the United States which funds medical research in vision and ophthalmology. He hosted its _Lights On_ telecast in 1960 and donated $100,000 ($1.04M in 2024) to establish the Bob Hope Fight for Sight Fund.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Fight_for_Sight-159) Hope recruited numerous top celebrities for the annual "Lights On" fundraiser. As an example, he hosted boxing champion [Joe Frazier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Frazier "Joe Frazier"), actress [Yvonne De Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yvonne_De_Carlo "Yvonne De Carlo"), and singer-actor [Sergio Franchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi "Sergio Franchi") as headliners for the April 25, 1971, show at Philharmonic Hall in [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee").[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Wilson_1971-160)

Hope settled into a home custom built for him in 1939 on an 87,000-square-foot (8,083 m 2) lot in the [Toluca Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toluca_Lake "Toluca Lake") section of [Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California") in the [San Fernando Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Valley "San Fernando Valley"). It was put on the market in late 2012.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMikailian2012-161)

The [Hope Residence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Residence "Hope Residence") is a 23,366-square-foot (2,171 m 2)[modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modernism "Modernism") home in [Palm Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs "Palm Springs"), built to resemble a volcano, that was designed in 1973 by [John Lautner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lautner "John Lautner"). The home is located above the city, with panoramic views of the [Coachella Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley "Coachella Valley") and the [San Jacinto Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jacinto_Mountains "San Jacinto Mountains"). It was put on the market for the first time in February 2013 with an asking price of $50 million,[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-NYTimes_February_2013-162) and sold to investor [Ron Burkle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Burkle "Ron Burkle") for just $13 million in November 2016.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-163)

### Advanced age and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Advanced age and death")]

At the age of 93, seven years before his death, Hope converted to [Catholicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholicism "Catholicism"), his wife's faith.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-seeing-stars_St_Charles-164)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-165)

In July 1997 at age 94, he attended the funeral of [James Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Stewart "James Stewart"), where many pointed out his frail appearance.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-166) At the age of 95, Hope made an appearance at the 50th anniversary of the [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") with [Milton Berle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Berle "Milton Berle") and [Sid Caesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sid_Caesar "Sid Caesar"). Contemporaries [Fay Wray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fay_Wray "Fay Wray") and [Gloria Stuart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_Stuart "Gloria Stuart") were also present.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Gallo_1998-167) Two years later, he was present at the opening of the Bob Hope Gallery of American Entertainment at the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress"). The Library of Congress has presented two major exhibitions about Hope's life: "Hope for America: Performers, Politics and Pop Culture" and "Bob Hope and American Variety".[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-myloc_hopeforamerica-168)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-loc_bobhope-169) He last made an appearance at the Hope Classic in 2000, where he hugged Swedish golfer [Jesper Parnevik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesper_Parnevik "Jesper Parnevik").[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-170)

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Bob_Hope_Grave.JPG/250px-Bob_Hope_Grave.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_Grave.JPG)

Graves of Bob and Dolores Hope, on the grounds of the Mission San Fernando Rey de España

In 1998, five years before his death, a prepared obituary written by [the Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Associated_Press "The Associated Press") was inadvertently released, resulting in Hope's death being announced on the floor of the [U.S. House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_of_Representatives "U.S. House of Representatives").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-c-span_June_1998-171)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998313-172) However, aside from increasing frailty, Hope remained in relatively good health until late in his old age.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002148-173) In June 2000 at age 97, he spent nearly a week in a California hospital being treated for [gastrointestinal bleeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrointestinal_bleeding "Gastrointestinal bleeding").[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-CNN_June_2000-174) In August 2001 at age 98, he spent close to two weeks in a hospital recovering from [pneumonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pneumonia "Pneumonia").[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-175)[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-guardian_September_2001-176)

Hope celebrated his 100th birthday on May 29, 2003.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-USA_Today_May_2003-177) To mark this event, the intersection of [Hollywood and Vine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_and_Vine "Hollywood and Vine") in Los Angeles was named "Bob Hope Square" and his centennial was declared "Bob Hope Day" in 35 states. Even at 100, Hope maintained his self-deprecating sense of humor, quipping, "I'm so old, they've canceled my [blood type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_type "Blood type")."[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-bbcdeath-178)

On July 27, 2003, Hope died of pneumonia at his home in [Toluca Lake, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toluca_Lake,_California "Toluca Lake, California").[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-bbcdeath-178) His grandson Zach Hope told [Soledad O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soledad_O'Brien "Soledad O'Brien") in an interview that, when asked at the end of his life where he wished to be buried, he said, "Surprise me".[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-CNN_July_29,_2003-179) His remains were temporarily placed in a mausoleum vault at the [San Fernando Mission Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Mission_Cemetery "San Fernando Mission Cemetery") before the construction of the Bob Hope Memorial Garden at the [San Fernando Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Mission "San Fernando Mission"), located next door to the cemetery, in Los Angeles. Dolores died in 2011, aged 102.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-180)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Doyle_2005-181) After his death, newspaper cartoonists worldwide paid tribute to his work for the USO, and some featured drawings of [Bing Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby"), who had died in 1977, welcoming Hope to Heaven.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-fac-assoc.org-182)

## Honors

*   Recipient of the Golden Plate Award of the [American Academy of Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Achievement "Academy of Achievement") in 1961[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-1)
*   Induction into the [National Association of Broadcasters Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Broadcasters_Hall_of_Fame "National Association of Broadcasters Hall of Fame") (for Radio) in 1977
*   Recipient of the [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors") in 1985
*   Induction into the [Television Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_Hall_of_Fame "Television Hall of Fame") in 1987
*   Induction into the [World Golf Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Golf_Hall_of_Fame "World Golf Hall of Fame") in 1983
*   Recipient of the [Arkansas Traveler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_Traveler_(honorary_title) "Arkansas Traveler (honorary title)")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-2)
*   Induction into [Omicron Delta Kappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omicron_Delta_Kappa "Omicron Delta Kappa"), the National Leadership Honor Society in 1992

*   [Ronald Reagan Freedom Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award "Ronald Reagan Freedom Award") (1997)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Times_Union_1997-6)

*   [1948 World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_World_Series "1948 World Series") Champion (as part owner of the [Cleveland Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians")).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-7)
*   Honorary mayor of [Palm Springs, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs,_California "Palm Springs, California") (1950s)
*   [Hasty Pudding Man of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasty_Pudding_Man_of_the_Year "Hasty Pudding Man of the Year") (first awardee, 1967)

*   _Honorary Veteran of the United States Armed Forces_, a tribute from the [United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") given in recognition of the entertainment he provided U.S. troops during [war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War "War") and peacekeeping missions (October 29, 1997)
*   Honorary [Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") (KBE) _In recognition of his contributions to film, to song, and to the entertainment of troops in the past._ (1998).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-BBC_1998-8) He had previously been appointed an Honorary Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in 1976.

*   The Honorable Order of [Kentucky Colonels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Colonel "Kentucky Colonel").
*   The [Grand Order of Water Rats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Order_of_Water_Rats "Grand Order of Water Rats").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-9)
*   Appointed a Knight Commander with Star of the [Order of St. Gregory the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_St._Gregory_the_Great "Order of St. Gregory the Great") by [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II") in 1998[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-LA_Times_1998-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Golf_Hall_of_Fame-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-NAB_Hall_of_Fame-12)
*   Hope became the 64th and only civilian recipient of the United States Air Force [Order of the Sword](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Sword_(United_States) "Order of the Sword (United States)") on June 10, 1980. *   In 1996 Hope was awarded the Naval Heritage Award by the [U S Navy Memorial Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_Memorial "Navy Memorial") for his support of the US Navy and military.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Lone_Sailor_Award-14)

### Memorials and tributes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Memorials and tributes")]

*   The [PGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGA_Tour "PGA Tour")'s [Bob Hope Chrysler Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Chrysler_Classic "Bob Hope Chrysler Classic"), which was an existing tournament (The Desert Classic) renamed in recognition of the comedian's lifelong passion for the game, 1966
*   The [Lorain-Carnegie Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorain-Carnegie_Bridge "Lorain-Carnegie Bridge") in Cleveland was renamed the Hope Memorial Bridge in 1983 (disputed as to whether it was meant to honor Hope, his stonemason father Harry, or the entire Hope Family)
*   _America's Tribute to Bob Hope_, a 1988 documentary taped at the [Palm Desert, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Desert,_California "Palm Desert, California"), Bob Hope Cultural Center[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-15)
*   In 1992, a Golden Palm Star on the [Palm Springs, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs,_California "Palm Springs, California"), [Walk of Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs_Walk_of_Stars "Palm Springs Walk of Stars") was dedicated to him.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Walk_of_Stars-16)
*   Bob Hope Drive, streets in both [Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California") (where there is also an airport named after him)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Daily_News_2010-17) and [Rancho Mirage, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Mirage,_California "Rancho Mirage, California"). The Rancho Mirage street is the location of [Eisenhower Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eisenhower_Medical_Center "Eisenhower Medical Center") which Hope and his wife were instrumental in creating.

_The Spirit of Bob Hope_ is a USAF C-17 Globemaster III that was named after Hope

*   [The United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_United_States_Air_Force "The United States Air Force") named a [C-17 Globemaster III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-17_Globemaster_III "C-17 Globemaster III") transport aircraft the _Spirit of Bob Hope_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Warplanes_Online_Community-18)
*   _Bob Hope: 50 Years of Hope_, an exhibition of Hope's service of entertaining the United States military at the [National Museum of the United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_the_United_States_Air_Force "National Museum of the United States Air Force") near [Dayton, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio "Dayton, Ohio")[](https://web.archive.org/web/20021028073736/http://www.wpafb.af.mil/museum/pa/nr021031.htm)
*   [Bob Hope Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Square "Bob Hope Square") (naming of the intersection at [Hollywood and Vine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_and_Vine "Hollywood and Vine") in Los Angeles to commemorate Hope's 100th birthday, May 29, 2003)
*   Memory Lane-Bob Hope Way (renaming of East 14th Street in [Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland") to commemorate Hope's 100th birthday in 2003)

On November 3, 2003 the [Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena_Airport "Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena Airport") Authority voted unanimously to rename the facility and on November 18, 2003 the [Glendale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glendale,_California "Glendale, California"), and [Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California") city councils voted unanimously to approve it. A rededication ceremony took place on December 17, the 100th anniversary of the [Wright brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_brothers "Wright brothers")' first powered flight.

*   [USNS _Bob Hope_(T-AKR-300)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Bob_Hope "MV Bob Hope") of the U.S. [Military Sealift Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Sealift_Command "Military Sealift Command") was named after the performer in 1997. It is one of very few [U.S. naval ships that were named after living people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._military_vessels_named_after_living_Americans "List of U.S. military vessels named after living Americans").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-FAS_2011-20)
*   _[Asteroid 2829 Bobhope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2829\_Bobhope "2829 Bobhope")_
*   The Bob Hope Theatre, an amateur theatre (although professional musicians receive payment) in [Eltham, London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eltham,_London "Eltham, London"), where he was born. He personally funded the theatre in 1980 to develop further projects for the venue.
*   [Blue plaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_plaque "Blue plaque") at 44, Craigton Road [Eltham, London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eltham,_London "Eltham, London"), Hope's place of birth.
*   The Bob Hope Theatre, an on-base movie theatre and lecture hall at [Marine Corps Air Station Miramar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Air_Station_Miramar "Marine Corps Air Station Miramar"), [San Diego, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego,_California "San Diego, California").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-mccsmiramar-21)
*   Hope had a long and close association with [Southern Methodist University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Methodist_University "Southern Methodist University") in [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas"). His donations of over $800,000 enabled the opening of the Bob Hope Theatre in the Owen Fine Arts Center of the [Meadows School of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meadows_School_of_the_Arts "Meadows School of the Arts"), and two theater scholarships and an award are named in his honor.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Southern_Methodist_University-22)
*   "The Bob Hope Chow Hall", the dining facility at [Camp Lemonnier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Lemonnier "Camp Lemonnier"), Djibouti, Africa.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-23)
*   Bob Hope Primary School, a [primary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_school "Primary school") located on Kadena US Air Force Base, in Okinawa, Japan.
*   The historic [Bob Hope Patriotic Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Patriotic_Hall "Bob Hope Patriotic Hall") building on [Figueroa Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Figueroa_Street "Figueroa Street") in [Los Angeles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County "Los Angeles County") was named in his honor on August 3, 2003, by the [Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County_Board_of_Supervisors "Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Molina_2009-24)
*   In a bill passed by Congress in 2008, the research library at the [Ellis Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Island "Ellis Island") Immigration Museum was renamed the Bob Hope Memorial Library.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Chan_2008-25)
*   At the U.S. Naval Academy, [Alumni Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alumni_Hall_(Navy) "Alumni Hall (Navy)") is home to the Bob Hope Performing Arts Center.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlake2010135-26)
*   In 2009 "A National Salute to Bob Hope and the Military" was dedicated in [San Diego, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego,_California "San Diego, California").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-portofsandiego_tribute-27)
